Development Workflow

Obviously you will have your own way of doing things. This section describes the workflow for which this project is configured.

Core Technology

This project uses:

  • Typescript

  • NodeJS (ts-node for smoother development workflow)

  • Jest (ts-jest is used to leverage ts-node during testing)

  • Docker

The main tool for configuring the project is npm (installed with NodeJS).

Documentation (this documentation), is written in ReStructuredText, processed using Sphinx.

Basic Development Cycle

Important

Before working on the code, create a new branch (git switch my_new_branch) to work on.

This will ensure you don’t run into problems later.

Use of Test Driven Development (TDD) is encouraged. So, first write a test to specify the change you are going to make. For a new feature this will typically be in a .spec.ts file. For a bug this will typically be in a .test.ts file alongside the code containing the bug.

Tip

Commit to your branch frequently (git add <your code> and git commit -m 'My awesome edits'). This provides a nice way to keep track of changes but more importantly gives you plenty a ‘checkpoints’ to roll-back to if you discover a problem with your current direction.

Write code for your changes.

Test using npm run test.

Tip

If you stage you changes (using git add) you can use npm run test:ci to limit the tests to those related to file in the staging index.

Repeat the write test/develop/test/refactor cycle until you have completed your change.

Commit the final changes to your repostory.

If you have installed act (see developer recommended installs) you can use it to run the CI chain locally. This helps identify any potential issues before you offer them into the official buildk

act

If you have followed the Project Code Management advice you will have a forked repository ready to prepare a Project Pull Request.

If you just want to use this modification yourself you can install directly from this local copy or you can push the change to your own forked repository’s main and a new npm package will be published.
